text:
sanjay: Heads-up — nightly perf for rwd-7b on tp=2 pp=2 showed a regression after the kernel-selector rollout. p95 up ~17% on small-request workloads.
ashley: ugh. which kernel selector build? and kv sharding config?
sanjay: rolled stable_v4 yesterday (auto-select new fused mha). Setup: tp=2 pp=2 dp=1, kv_shard=roundrobin-layer, batching=continuous (favor long seqs). Workload is many concurrent short requests (1-16 tokens). Before: p50 42ms / p95 128ms / p99 320ms. After: p50 55ms / p95 150ms / p99 370ms.
evie: can you paste the profiler summary? sounds like comm/compute overlap broke.
sanjay: profiler top-line:
  - comm time: 42%
  - compute time: 48%
  - idle/wait: 10%
  top kernels by time: fused_mha_v4, kv_lookup, cuda_memcpy_async
  note: NCCL allreduce count per step increased (more frequent small allreduces)
noah: batching heuristics change could make the runtime emit smaller groups, causing more sync points. KV hit-rate drop will amplify cross-GPU lookups.
leo: hypothesis: fused_mha_v4 changes kernel launch ordering so KV cache lookups are no longer overlapped with comm. With roundrobin-layer sharding we end up doing cross-TP lookups that need nccl ops to materialize, increasing small allreduces.
leo: quick repro command I used: 
  export RW_KERNEL_SELECTOR=stable_v4
  ./bench_tool --model rwd-7b --tp 2 --pp 2 --kv-policy roundrobin-layer --qps 1200 --seq-dist "short"
ashley: can we try local-affinity kv policy? shard cache by tp slice and replicate hot keys across pp boundaries. That should reduce cross-tile lookups at cost of extra memory.
perf-bot: alert: perf-regression detected — nightly rwd-7b tp2pp2 (2026-03-17T03:12Z) P95 +17% (baseline 128ms -> 150ms). Linked: ci/bench/2014567800
sanjay: launching two canaries: (A) revert kernel selector to stable_v3, (B) keep v4 but switch kv-policy=local_affinity + replicate-top-5pct. Will post numbers in ~30m.
sanjay: canary A results: p50 43ms p95 130ms p99 330ms (basically baseline).
sanjay: canary B results: p50 48ms p95 132ms p99 345ms. KV hit-rate improved 78% -> 72% and NCCL allreduce count dropped ~22%.
evie: nice — shows regression is interaction between the new fused kernel ordering and cross-shard KV lookups. Reverting kernel fixes perf but local_affinity mitigates without full revert.
noah: we should add a synthetic test that targets short random-prefix workloads to catch this class of regressions. Suggested reproducer snippet:
  for i in range(2000):
    send_request(model='rwd-7b', prompt=random_prefix(1,8), max_tokens=8)
  measure p50/p95/p99 over steady-state
ashley: agree. open perf issue with experiment results and mark for next kernel-selector release gating. I'll also run memory/cost estimate for replicating top keys.
leo: I'll follow up to add a kernel-selector invariant: prefer ordering that preserves kv lookup/comm overlap for short-request workloads (or fall back to stable if kv hit-rate < 60%).
sanjay: thanks all — filing issue now and will attach NCCL traces + profiler flame. :thumbsup:
